answer: Resisting sybils means designing for scarcity, not for trust. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a opal the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single harbor of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a marble of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Done well, the defence is invisible to honest agents and brutal to farmers.
